title: Bennett numerical normal-flatness criterion without reducedness
statement:
Let $F$ be a field and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative $F$-algebra essentially of finite type (a localization of a finitely generated $F$-algebra) [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a prime ideal such that $A=R/I$ is a regular local ring, and set $d=\dim A$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Write $R_I$ for localization at $I$, whose maximal ideal is $IR_I$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and define
$$h_R(n)=\operatorname{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}),\qquad h_{R_I}(n)=\operatorname{length}_{R_I}(R_I/(IR_I)^{n+1}),\quad n\ge0$$
[def-weil-pbc-module-length]. For sequences put $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n f(j)$. Then
$$\operatorname{gr}_I R\text{ is flat over }A\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h_R=\Lambda^d h_{R_I},$$
where $\operatorname{gr}_I R=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}I^j/I^{j+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] and flatness means that tensoring injections of $A$-modules with this graded ring preserves injectivity [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The case $I=0$ is allowed. No reducedness is assumed on $R$.

source.place: Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, Canonical embedded and non-embedded resolution of singularities for excellent two-dimensional schemes, March 12 2009 preprint, section 2 (X any excellent scheme, D a reduced closed subscheme; no reducedness of X), Theorem 2.3(1) iff (2), printed p.29, which is Bennett [Be], Theorem (3). The source compares degree-wise Hilbert functions H^{(0)}_{O_{X,x}}=H^{(codim)}_{O_{X,y}}; applying one summation gives the length convention here, with codim = dim A. Purely local; includes a nilpotent prime centre. Read online at https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/13766/1/MP32.pdf; archival copy WANTED. The document field names the ancestor (BMT) source only. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text:
Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m/I$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and $G_j=I^j/I^{j+1}$. The ring $A$ is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Each $I^j$ is finite over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], so $G_j$ is finite over $A$, since $I$ annihilates it. Define $r_j=\dim_K(K\otimes_A G_j)$ and $\mu_j=\dim_k(G_j/\mathfrak aG_j)$. Localize $0\to I^{j+1}\to I^j\to G_j\to0$ at $R\setminus I$ using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. The localized quotient of $R/I$ is $K$, so
$$K\otimes_A G_j\simeq (IR_I)^j/(IR_I)^{j+1}.$$
Thus $r_j=g_{R_I}(j)$, where $g_T(j)=\dim_{T/\mathfrak m_T}\mathfrak m_T^j/\mathfrak m_T^{j+1}$. All these dimensions are finite.

source.place: Tags 00NP (lemma-regular-domain), 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), and 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); elementary identification of the localized ideal powers and residue field.

proof.text: For later use, a finite $A$-module $M$ with $r=\dim_K(K\otimes_A M)$ and $\mu=\dim_k(M/\mathfrak aM)$ is free if $\mu=r$. Indeed, lifts of a residue basis give a surjection $A^\mu\to M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators]. If $L$ is its kernel, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] makes $K\otimes_A L$ the kernel of a surjection between $K$-spaces of the same dimension, hence zero. An element of $L\subseteq A^\mu$ which vanishes after localization is killed by a nonzero element of the domain $A$, and therefore is zero coordinate by coordinate. Thus $L=0$. Conversely $M\simeq A^r$ has $\mu=r$, directly from the standard basis. This includes rank zero.

source.place: Tags 00DV (lemma-NAK, local generators) and 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); elementary kernel argument over the domain A.

proof.text:
For $T=R$ or $R_I$, the filtration of $T/\mathfrak m_T^{n+1}$ by its maximal-ideal powers has successive factors $\mathfrak m_T^j/\mathfrak m_T^{j+1}$ for $0\le j\le n$. A basis of each such residue-field vector space gives a composition series with that many one-dimensional simple factors. Repeated use of [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] therefore gives $h_T=\Lambda g_T$. On integer sequences set $\Delta f(0)=f(0)$ and $\Delta f(n)=f(n)-f(n-1)$ for $n>0$. Telescoping gives $\Delta\Lambda f=f=\Lambda\Delta f$. Consequently the desired numerical equality is equivalent to
$$g_R=\Lambda^d r,\qquad r(j)=r_j.$$
This equivalence concerns all entries, not just eventual Hilbert polynomials.

source.place: Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive); maximal-ideal filtration and telescoping. Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, Theorem 2.3(2), uses the degree-wise convention g rather than h.

proof.text: Write $C=\widehat R$ for maximal-ideal completion, $J=IC$, $D=\widehat A$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mC$, and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak aD$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] both completions are Noetherian and complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] they are local with maximal ideals $\mathfrak n,\mathfrak p$ and common residue field $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], $C/\mathfrak n^q\simeq R/\mathfrak m^q$ for all $q\ge1$. Taking kernels of successive quotient maps gives $g_C=g_R$. The ring $D$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] and has dimension $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension-eq]. No completion of $R_I$ is used.

The quotient-completion map of [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] identifies $C/J=D$, and identifies the image of the completion of $I^j\hookrightarrow R$ with $I^jC=J^j$. Exact completion [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] applied to $0\to I^{j+1}\to I^j\to G_j\to0$ therefore identifies
$$H_j:=J^j/J^{j+1}\simeq\widehat{G_j}\simeq D\otimes_A G_j.$$
For the last isomorphism use [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] over $A$: the $\mathfrak m$-adic filtration on $G_j$ equals its $\mathfrak a$-adic filtration since $IG_j=0$. The reduction statement of [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] gives $H_j/\mathfrak pH_j\simeq G_j/\mathfrak aG_j$. In particular, if $G_j\simeq A^{r_j}$ then $H_j\simeq D^{r_j}$, while $\dim_k H_j/\mathfrak pH_j=\mu_j$ without any freeness assumption.

source.place: Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated). All modules completed in this step are finite.

proof.text: Choose a coefficient ring $k_0\subset C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists]. Because $C$ contains the field $F$, its characteristic equals the characteristic of its residue field. The coefficient ring's maximal ideal $p k_0$ is consequently zero, so $k_0$ is a field and $k_0\simeq k$. Its image in $D$ is again a coefficient field. Choose $d$ generators $\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_d$ of $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-trf-regular-complete-coefficient-coordinates], $\theta:k_0[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]\to D$, $T_i\mapsto\bar t_i$, is an isomorphism. Lift them to $t_i\in\mathfrak n$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] to obtain $E:k_0[[T]]\to C$. The composite of $E$ with $C\to D$ is $\theta$ by the explicit evaluation formula. Thus $s=E\theta^{-1}:D\to C$ is a section. Regard $D$ as a subring by $s$; then $\mathfrak n=J+\mathfrak pC$. No $F$-linearity of this section, and no separability of $k/F$, is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tags 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), 0326 (definition-coefficient-ring and following equicharacteristic discussion), 0C0S (lemma-regular-complete-containing-coefficient-field); adic evaluation as in More on Algebra 07NL/07NN.

proof.text:
Fix $N\ge1$ and assume only that $G_j$ is free over $A$ for $j<N$. Put $B=C/J^{N+1}$ and $Q=JB$. The section of step 6 makes $B$ a $D$-algebra. We have $Q^{N+1}=0$, $Q^j/Q^{j+1}=H_j$, $Q^N=H_N$, and $\mathfrak b:=Q+\mathfrak pB=\mathfrak nB$. Apply [lem-per-split-nilpotent-filtration-graded-piece], since step 5 gives $H_j\cong D^{r_j}$ for $j<N$. As $J^{N+1}\subseteq\mathfrak n^{N+1}$, the quotient $C\to B$ preserves the degree-$N$ maximal-ideal graded piece. Thus
$$\mathfrak n^N/\mathfrak n^{N+1}\cong H_N/\mathfrak pH_N\oplus\bigoplus_{j<N}(\mathfrak p^{N-j}/\mathfrak p^{N-j+1})^{\oplus r_j}.$$
Let $c_d(q)$ count monomials of degree $q$ in $d$ variables, with $c_0(0)=1$ and $c_0(q)=0$ for $q>0$. Under the power-series coordinates of step 6, $\mathfrak p^q$ consists of series with no terms below degree $q$: assign each exponent of degree at least $q$ to a degree-$q$ divisor and factor out that monomial (only finitely many divisors occur). Degree-$q$ coefficient extraction then gives a basis of $\mathfrak p^q/\mathfrak p^{q+1}$ on those monomials. Taking dimensions, with steps 4--5, yields
$$g_R(N)=\mu_N+\sum_{j<N}r_jc_d(N-j).$$
In particular, this formula does not assume $G_N$ free.

source.place: Agent-written finite filtered-module calculation, using only lifts of bases and expansion of powers of a sum of ideals; not a quoted Stacks theorem. This isolates the calculation in steps 7--8 of the accepted agent proof of lem-trf-bennett-normal-flat-numerical-criterion, which applies without reducedness. Natural-language proof retained in report.md.

proof.text:
For any sequence $r$, define its convolution with $c_d$ in degree $n$ by $\sum_{j=0}^n r_jc_d(n-j)$. A monomial in $d+1$ variables is uniquely a monomial in $d$ variables times a power of the last variable, whence $c_{d+1}(q)=\sum_{i=0}^q c_d(i)$. Interchanging two finite sums shows that replacing $c_d$ by $c_{d+1}$ replaces the convolution by its partial sums. Starting with $c_0$ therefore gives
$$(\Lambda^d r)(n)=\sum_{j=0}^n r_jc_d(n-j).$$
In particular, $c_d(0)=1$ for every $d\ge0$, so the coefficient of $r_n$ is always one. This includes $d=0$.

source.place: Agent-written equicharacteristic proof of the Bennett criterion; explicit calculation below.

proof.text: Assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$. Each $G_j$ is a direct summand of $G$. It is flat: for an injection $U\hookrightarrow V$, a kernel element in $U\otimes_A G_j$ embeds by the split inclusion in $U\otimes_A G$, where it is zero by flatness, and the split projection gives its original value zero. Each $G_j$ is finite by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] makes it free over the local ring $A$. Its rank is $r_j$ after tensoring with $K$, and hence $\mu_j=r_j$. Apply the formula of step 7 for every $N\ge1$ and step 8 to obtain $g_R(N)=(\Lambda^d r)(N)$. Degree zero also agrees: $g_R(0)=1=r_0$. Thus $g_R=\Lambda^d r$, and step 3 yields $h_R=\Lambda^d h_{R_I}$.

source.place: Tag 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local); flatness of the individual graded summands is proved directly from the tensor-injection definition, followed by the finite calculation of steps 7--10.

proof.text:
Conversely, assume $h_R=\Lambda^d h_{R_I}$, so $g_R=\Lambda^d r$ by step 3. We prove by induction on $N$ that $G_N$ is free of rank $r_N$. At $N=0$, $G_0=A$ and $r_0=1$. If all degrees below $N\ge1$ are free, steps 7 and 8 give
$$\mu_N+\sum_{j<N}r_jc_d(N-j)=g_R(N)=(\Lambda^d r)(N)=r_N+\sum_{j<N}r_jc_d(N-j).$$
Cancel the finite sum to get $\mu_N=r_N$. The explicit kernel argument in step 2 makes $G_N$ free of rank $r_N$, completing the induction. The induction uses no assumed freeness in degree $N$; that degree was the unrestricted summand $M$ in step 7.

source.place: Agent-written equicharacteristic proof of the Bennett criterion; explicit calculation below.

proof.text: Choose the bases just obtained for all $G_j$. Their disjoint union, with each vector labelled by its degree, is an $A$-basis of $G=\bigoplus_jG_j$, since every element of a direct sum has finite support and relations separate degree by degree. For an injection $U\hookrightarrow V$, the basis identifies tensoring with $G$ with a direct sum of copies of that injection. A finite-support tuple which maps to zero has every coordinate zero; hence this direct sum map is injective. This is exactly the flatness required in the statement. Both implications are now established. No nontrivial-centre hypothesis occurred, so the proof also applies to $I=0$; if $I=\mathfrak m$, then $d=0$ and the numerical assertion is the identity $h_R=h_R$.
